## How to use this catalog

1. Cross-reference a DBC message above against the SysVar tree to find the
   matching namespace (naming conventions vary by project -- look for a
   namespace whose name matches the message, or child `SYSVARS`/`TIMINGS`
   namespaces).
2. Read/write via:
   ```powershell
   python -m canoe signal sysvar read "<Namespace>" "<Variable>"
   python -m canoe signal sysvar write "<Namespace>" "<Variable>" <value>
   ```
3. If a sibling `TIMINGS` namespace exists next to the signal's namespace,
   check `EnableCyclic`/`MasterCyclicOnOff` -- if 0 (or absent), you likely
   need to write `SendOnce=1` to actually transmit the value onto the bus
   after writing the SysVar. If `EnableCyclic=1` already, the write
   propagates automatically on the next cyclic tick -- no extra trigger
   needed.
4. Verify via `python -m canoe signal bus read "<Message>" "<Signal>"`
   (works even with no SysVar link at all, for ECU Tx/feedback signals).
5. For multi-step/timed test cases, use
   `python -m canoe sequence ramp` / `sequence run-spec` (see the generic
   `canoe-interface` skill) instead of writing a new script per test case.
